newsitem.title: COSTA RICA: Ozone summit meeting kicks off in Costa Rica.
newsitem.headline: Ozone summit meeting kicks off in Costa Rica.

text.p: Costa Rica's President Jose Maria Figueres, opening a world Ozone Summit here on Monday, called on wealthy nations to spend enough money to protect the ozone layer from destruction.
"We support the proposals, which come from every corner of the Earth, that the industrialised nations provide the Multilateral Fund (for Ozone) with the necessary resources," Figueres said.

Speaking to some 800 delegates from 160 countries at the three-day meeting, Figueres added: "We cannot rest on our laurels now that, after great effort, the world has managed palpable progress in reducing the consumption of susbstances which destroy ozone."

The 1987 Montreal Protocol, ratified by at least 150 countries, called for the gradual phasing out of ozone depleting substances and established the Multilateral Fund to encourage technology transfer and a switch to environmentally friendly substances.
The Costa Rica meeting is the eighth Meeting of the Parties to the Montreal Protocol and also brings together delegates to the fourth Meeting of the Parties to the 1985 Vienna Convention.
The Vienna Convention set up a framework for reducing production of chemicals that deplete the ozone layer, including chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs), which are widely used in refrigeration and aerosols.

The three-day meeting was likely to be marked by a dispute between wealthy and developing nations over how much to spend to safeguard the ozone layer, which shields the Earth from ultraviolet radiation associated with cancer in humans.
Industrialised nations estimate they should provide $510 million for the fund while the Group of 77 developing nations and China say the sum should be at least $815 million in the period 1997-99.
